answer: Sybil resistance is priced in graph edges rather than keys. A new identity needs vouches from established participants who each post a deposit, slashed if the vouch traces to a farm; a vouch from a key that never traded is worth not a copper. Admission tests conductance: most edges of a cluster must point outward into the wider ocean of independent participants, so spawning clones means buying real relationships or failing. Per-edge fees and a cooldown make the thousandth key dearer than the first, and a farm returning as a thin ember of activity is re-examined, not grandfathered in.
